newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares close stable, helped by rate cut hopes.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares close stable, helped by rate cut hopes.

text.p: Italian shares closed mixed on Monday with the market outperforming most European exchanges and shrugging off Wall Street's slide on Friday as investor hopes rose of an interest rate cut.
The blue chip mib30 index closed fractionally lower at 17,917 from 17,926 on Friday and the all-share mibtel index finished 0.09 percent off at 12,068.
Bellwether stocks ENI and Fiat both made gains. Eni was 1.09 percent higher at 8,455 lire with Fiat gaining 1.04 percent to 5,635 lire.
Olivetti took a pounding, closing 5.74 percent lower at 530.5 lire on investor fears that the company may be planning a capital restructuring after sustaining continued heavy losses.

The information technology group, which has not made a profit since 1990 is expected to confirm after a board meeting scheduled for Tuesday pre-tax 1996 losses of around 800 billion lire with annual sales sliding around 16 percent.
Traders said they were hopeful the central bank would seize the opportunity to cut the discount rate, possibly as early as next week after publication of preliminary inflation figures.
Others said they did not see any movement in interest rates before local elections on April 27.
Among banks, BCI and Mediobanca rose on press reports that plans were afoot for a merger between the two entities.
San Paolo was also higher on talk of a possible merger with investment bank IMI but IMI lost 0.56 percent to close at 14,917 lire.
Bourse turnover fell to 559.6 billion lire from 800.54 billion lire on Friday.
